text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • kv-cache pressure (prefill vs decode imbalance) — elevated p95/p99 tail latencies on streaming endpoints in us-west-2. Severity: S3. Auto-ops runbook attached.

sam: saw the alert. p99 on streaming-routes jumped to ~2.4s from 350ms around 21:10 UTC.

mira: looking at dashboards now — KV eviction rate spiked at 21:05, slab reuse down. Streaming stalls correlate with prefill queue depth rising.

rahul: upload of sample traces to s3://redwood-incidents/6301298765/traces.tar.gz — includes a tail session that shows many prefill requests blocking decode workers.

sam: customer-impact check — querying logs for 5m before/after. Early numbers: ~3.2% of streaming requests experienced >1s tail; major customers A & C reported timeouts on long sessions.

devon: infra note — memfrag on kv-shards 7/8. Prefill goroutines allocate large buffers; decode uses GPU mem mapping but waits on KVS reads. Looks like prefill creates hot keys that trigger eviction waves.

kim: can we route streaming traffic to warm nodes while we mitigate? we have a standby pool in us-west-2b.

mira: quick mitigation plan: 1) enable kv-prefill-throttle at 0.5x via feature-flag (reduces prefetch parallelism), 2) increase slab reclaim interval to reduce aggressive evictions, 3) temporarily route 20% traffic to standby pool, 4) watch p99 for 10m.

sam: +1 to plan. who can flip the feature-flag? @deploy-bot, can you run the console change? will need a fast rollback route.

deploy-bot: I can flip kv-prefill-throttle for the us-west-2 cluster. running: `POST /api/v1/flags/kv-prefill-throttle?action=enable&scale=0.5&region=us-west-2` — will take ~30s to propagate.

mira: also please run `PATCH /api/v1/serving/pools/standby/route` to add a temporary 20% weight for streaming routes.

deploy-bot: throttle enabled. standby pool weight set to 20%.

rahul: immediate effect on prefill queue depth — down ~60% in the graphs. eviction rate falling but slab fragmentation still high.

sam: new p95/p99 numbers: p95 back to 420ms, p99 down to 850ms after 3m. Customer-facing SLOs still at risk but trending good.

kim: we should also disable prefill for extremely long contexts (>8k tokens) while we do deeper fix; that avoids creating huge prefetch footprints.

devon: agree. adding a temporary rule: `if context_len > 8000: prefill=false` — patch ready. Who wants to apply?

mira: i'll push that rule to a canary scope (10% of long sessions) first.

sam: also need to coordinate oncall handoff. I'm wrapping initial mitigation and will hand to Mira for follow-up analysis and postmortem. @mira you taking next shift?

mira: taking handoff. I'll keep the incident open for 2h and own the RCA. Sam, please update pagerduty that oncall has been handed off.

sam: done. PD note: "Handoff to Mira for follow-up — mitigations applied: kv-prefill-throttle, route shift, long-context prefill disable canary. Monitoring p99." link: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/6301298765

support-ledger: we logged affected customer accounts and opened support tickets for A/C with subject: "Investigating elevated streaming latency — mitigation in progress". CS will send an interim email.

mira: next steps for RCA: - gather heap profiles from kv-shards 7/8, - analyze timeline of prefill vs decode latencies, - check kernel-level OOM/kern logs for page reclaim churn, - simulate prefill-heavy workload in staging for repro.

rahul: I'll extract flame graphs and upload to the incident bucket. Also will run a targeted eviction policy test in staging to measure tail p99 impact.

devon: medium-term fix candidates: smarter prefill backpressure (adaptive to eviction rate), split slab for prefill vs decode keys, and a prefill-key lifetime TTL to avoid hot churn.

mira: agreed. I'll own the postmortem and schedule a design follow-up with storage and runtime teams. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre for design sync.

sam: thanks all. final note before I hand off: if p99 creeps above 1.5s again, escalate to S2 and start emergency scale-up of standby pool to 50%.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED • mitigations applied by sam and deploy-bot. status: stabilizing. assigned: mira (lead), sam (initial responder), rahul (traces), devon (infra), kim (cs).
